## **61: ### next.js architecture updates for chrome workspaces goal:...**
Date: 2:36pm PST, May 27, 2026
Model: Gemini 3.1 flash
Git branch: LiveAPI

**🥸 Hans**  
<USER_REQUEST>
### Next.js Architecture Updates for Chrome Workspaces

Goal: Force high-fidelity source map generation. Next.js defaults to eval-based maps in development, which break DevTools file binding.

* Update root `next.config.ts` (or `.js` / `.mjs`).
* Override Webpack `devtool` for client-side development.
* Forces full `source-map` generation instead of `eval-source-map`.
* Note: Slightly increases Hot Module Replacement (HMR) rebuild times.
* Requires dev server restart after applying.
* [Reference: Next.js Custom Webpack Config](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/next-config-js/webpack)

**Implementation:**

```typescript
import type { NextConfig } from 'next';

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  webpack: (config, { dev, isServer }) => {
    // Force high-fidelity source maps for Chrome Workspace binding
    if (dev && !isServer) {
      config.devtool = 'source-map';
    }
    return config;
  },
};

export default nextConfig;

```
</USER_REQUEST>

**🤖 Gemini:**  
The project's color variables are centralized in `app/globals.css` using a two-tier architecture. Static hex values are first defined as base primitive variables (e.g., `--primitive-blue-500`), which then bubble up into semantic variables (e.g., `--color-bg`, `--color-alert-info-bg`) that use the native CSS `light-dark()` function to automatically map light and dark values depending on the `color-scheme` property. Custom palettes like the blue mode are handled via an `html[data-color-scheme="blue"]` block in the same file, which simply overrides those semantic variables with new `light-dark()` configurations.

```javascript
);

```

5: # Chat Logger Skill
6: 
7: Syncs repo history to `user/user_log.md` and provides an automated, style-preserving sync to a Google Doc. It aggregates new interactions locally, overwrites them to Drive via native markdown conversion (which perfectly synchronizes existing summaries and new logs), and restores the exact template styles and table of contents anchors.
8: 
9: ## ⚙️ Initial Setup
10: 
11: To configure this skill to sync with Google Docs, you must set up the Google Cloud SDK (`gcloud`) and authorize it with correct scopes:
12: 
13: 1.  **Authorize Application Default Credentials (ADC):**
14:     ```bash
15:     gcloud auth application-default login --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/documents,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
16:     ```
17: 2.  **Enable Required APIs on Sandbox Project:**
18:     ```bash
19:     gcloud services enable docs.googleapis.com drive.googleapis.com --project=google.com:henge-sandbox
20:     ```
21: 
22: ---
23: 
24: ## Instructions
25: 
26: ### 1. Sync Messages (Local & Google Doc)
27: Run the synchronization script. By default, if the log file has been synced before, it will automatically update the Google Doc. You can also force a sync with `--sync-gdoc` or by setting the environment variable `SYNC_GOOGLE_DOC=true`:
28: 
29:

48: -   **Tracking Existing Docs:** To avoid creating duplicate documents, the script parses the document ID from the metadata block at the bottom of `user_log.md`:

2: name: chat-logger
3: description: Syncs repository history to user/user_log.md and optionally uploads a styled single-tab Google Doc natively, extracting intent and providing a summarized interaction log.
4: ---
5: # Chat Logger Skill
6: 
7: Syncs repo history to `user/user_log.md` and provides an automated, style-preserving sync to a Google Doc. It aggregates new interactions locally, overwrites them to Drive via native markdown conversion (which perfectly synchronizes existing summaries and new logs), and restores the exact template styles and table of contents anchors.
8: 
9: ## ⚙️ Initial Setup
10: 
11: To configure this skill to sync with Google Docs, you must set up the Google Cloud SDK (`gcloud`) and authorize it with correct scopes:
12: 
13: 1.  **Authorize Application Default Credentials (ADC):**
14:     ```bash
15:     gcloud auth application-default login --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/documents,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
16:     ```
17: 2.  **Enable Required APIs on Sandbox Project:**
18:     ```bash
19:     gcloud services enable docs.googleapis.com drive.googleapis.com --project=google.com:henge-sandbox
20:     ```
21: 
22: ---
23: 
24: ## Instructions
25: 
26: ### 1. Sync Messages (Local & Google Doc)
27: Run the synchronization script. By default, if the log file has been synced before, it will automatically update the Google Doc. You can also force a sync with `--sync-gdoc` or by setting the environment variable `SYNC_GOOGLE_DOC=true`:
28: 
29: 
<truncated 1431 bytes>
Runs a robust `batchUpdate` Docs API call to re-apply the template's background color, margins, text justification, typography (EB Garamond & Trebuchet MS), explicitly forces paragraph indents/alignment on the content to prevent Drive import override, and meticulously updates all literal URL anchor links (e.g., `#slug`) to map natively to Google Doc heading IDs (`h.xxxx`).
48: -   **Tracking Existing Docs:** To avoid creating duplicate documents, the script parses the document ID from the metadata block at the bottom of `user_log.md`:
49:     `* **Google Doc ID:** <document_id>` (If missing, it automatically searches Drive for an existing document with the exact title before creating a new copy).
50: 
51: ### 3. Intent Summarizer
52: -   **Consult Metadata:** Check `Total Messages` and `Summarized Up To` in `user/user_log.md`.
53: -   **Trigger:** Act as the Intent Summarizer if:
54:     1.  `Summarized Up To` is 0 or missing.
55:     2.  `Total Messages` - `Summarized Up To` > 4.
56:     3.  The user explicitly requests it.
57: -   **Surgical Update:**
58:     -   Locate start line using `grep -n "## **N:" user/user_log.md` (where N = Summarized Up To + 1). Note that each prompt block has an HTML anchor `<a id="prompt-N"></a>` on the line immediately preceding the heading.
59:     -   Generate a 5-8 word **intent** summary for each new prompt, ensuring you strip any XML tags like `<user_request>`.
60:     -   Use the `replace` tool to update the metadata block at the bottom, setting `Summarized Up To: {Total Messages}`.
61:     -   *If Google Doc ID is present, the next sync execution will push these new summaries to Google Docs.*
62: 
63: ### 4. Reformatter
64: When the user asks to "reformat" a markdown file:
65: -   Run: `python3 ~/.gemini/skills/chat-logger/sync.py --reformat [path/to/file.md]`
66: -   Once finished, perform the **Intent Summarizer** workflow to update descriptions and sync back to Google Docs if enabled.
67:
